amendments.rule: An English particle or adverb that realizes a Greek **preverb** rides inside the compound verb's own unit and is never `added`, as a discontinuous realization under rule 15 where the ASV separates them: `ἐξῆλθεν` → *went forth*, `ἐξέβαλον` → *cast out*, `ἀνέβη` → *went up*, `ἐπεβίβασαν` → *set thereon* at LUK.19.35, `προσηργάσατο` → *hath made more* at LUK.19.16, `ἀπολάβωσιν` → *receive again* at LUK.6.34. The head is the English word glossing the **verbal root**, never the particle. The corpus is unanimous: 963 units across 141 chapters carry such a particle and every one of them is `aligned`, none `added`, and the head stands on the verb word in all but one class. This is scoped to a particle **no other source token stands to answer to**. Where an expressed preposition does answer to it — because the particle is part of that preposition's own English gloss, as *out* is of `ἐκ` → *out of* — the whole English prepositional expression is the preposition's, headed on the prepositional word, and the compound verb keeps only its verb word: `ἔξελθε ἐξ αὐτοῦ` → *come* and *out of*, `ἐξῆλθεν ἐξ αὐτοῦ` → *came* and *out of*, as `εἰσελθὼν εἰς` → *entered* and *into* and `ἀπῆλθεν ἀπ᾽ αὐτοῦ` → *departed* and *from* do. Rule 36 is what decides that and says it in terms: an English preposition governing a prepositional phrase realizes the Greek preposition and not the verb it depends on, even where English idiom makes the verb phrasal, and a preposition is left `unrepresented` only where English realizes it nowhere at all — so do not leave such a preposition a bare *of* while the verb takes the *out*. A **noncompositional prepositional phrase** standing in the same clause answers to the particle in the same way, and the single English word is that phrase's rather than the preverb's: `συνήχθησαν ἐπὶ τὸ αὐτό` → *were gathered together* gives *were gathered* to the verb and *together* to `ἐπί` + `αὐτό` as one `noncompositional` unit under rule 45, the intervening article standing `unrepresented` under rule 93, as MAT.22.34 and ACT.4.26 read it and as ACT.2.44 reads the same phrase where no compound verb competes. Where no such phrase stands, the preverb keeps the word in the ordinary way, which is why `συνηγμένοι` → *gathered together* and `συνήχθησαν` → *were gathered together* keep *together* inside the verb's own unit. A preverb whose sense the following preposition's gloss does **not** carry keeps this rule's ordinary treatment, which is why `ἀναβαίνων ἐκ τοῦ ὕδατος` → *coming up out of the water* gives *up* to the participle and *out of* to `ἐκ` in one clause, and why `ἐκβάλλει … εἰς` → *driveth … forth* and *into* does. Rule 94 decides only whether the preposition and the word it governs form one unit, and does not decide where the particle goes. Where the compound verb governs a bare dative or genitive that the ASV writes with an English preposition, that preposition realizes the case government and rides with the governed word under rules 21, 36 and 69, as MRK.14.65 has it and as ACT.4.1 `ἐπέστησαν αὐτοῖς` → *came* and *upon them* and ACT.4.3 `ἐπέβαλον … αὐτοῖς` → *laid* and *on them* do. The one exception is an idiom that leaves no English verb word to head on at all: `Ἆρον` → *away with him* at JHN.19.15 and `Αἶρε` → *away with* at LUK.23.18 head on *away*, because nothing else was written.
amendments.why: Rule 106's exception was written for a preposition whose own English gloss carries the particle (out of, into), and its opening scope clause said no Greek *preposition* stands to answer to the particle. It did not consider a noncompositional prepositional phrase — ἐπὶ τὸ αὐτό — whose single English word carries the same sense as the preverb of the verb governing it. Rule 106 is recent and absolute in tone, so a later pass meeting συνήχθησαν ἐπὶ τὸ αὐτό would be pushed to give together to the verb and strand the phrase, or to split it, both of which rules 45 and 93 forbid. The corpus decides it: ἐπὶ αὐτό → together is noncompositional at MAT.22.34, where συνήχθησαν stands and the ASV writes together once, and at ACT.2.44 where no compound verb competes; ACT.4.26 follows them. The addition widens the scope clause from *preposition* to *source token*, states the phrase case with its evidence, and says in terms that where no such phrase stands the preverb keeps the word — so 4:27 and 4:31 are untouched. The MRK.14.65 sentence is extended with the two ACT.4 datives that exercise it, and nothing else in the rule is altered.

conventions: An ἐπι- compound verb governing a bare dative — ἐπέστησαν αὐτοῖς at 4:1, ἐπέβαλον … αὐτοῖς at 4:3 — is read under rule 106's closing clause: the English upon or on realizes the dative's case government and rides with the governed pronoun, and the verb keeps only its verb word. Do not read it as the preverb's own realization, which would leave the pronoun with no case preposition at all.

The συν- preverb of συνάγω is realized by together inside the verb's own unit (4:27 συνήχθησαν → were gathered together, 4:31 συνηγμένοι → gathered together). Where ἐπὶ τὸ αὐτό stands in the same clause and the ASV writes together once (4:26), that word is the prepositional phrase's instead, as one noncompositional unit on ἐπί + αὐτό with the intervening article unrepresented under rule 93, and συνήχθησαν keeps only were gathered. MAT.22.34 and ACT.2.44 are the precedent.

In τοὺς πόδας τῶν ἀποστόλων → the apostles' feet (4:35, 4:37) the article governing πόδας is unrepresented, the English possessive already occupying its determiner slot under rule 20, while the article governing the genitive possessor keeps its own the. A reference comparison reports the first article as represented in BSB; that report is not a correction.

A substantival article before a participle keeps only the pronoun even where the ASV writes that which: τῷ takes that and γεγονότι takes which was done (rule 32). Rule 90 relaxes this only for a single relativizer, and rule 77's finding that τὸ → that which heads on that is a claim about the head, not licence to take the pair whole as one unit.

report: One real cross-verse split, found and patched. The chapter analyses a substantival article before a participle five times. Four split under rule 32 — 4:4 τῶν → of them / ἀκουσάντων → that heard, 4:21 οἱ → they, 4:24 οἱ → they, 4:32 τῶν → of them / πιστευσάντων → that believed — and 4:32 and 4:34 do the same where the article also supplies a nominal. ACT.4.21's ἐπὶ τῷ γεγονότι alone gave the article both words, τῷ → that which, leaving the participle a bare was done. Patched to τῷ → that and γεγονότι → which was done headed on done.

The verse's note cited rule 77, but rule 77's nine τὸ → that which units are a claim about the head, not about the unit's edge. Rule 22 sends the participle case to rule 32 in terms, and rule 90 relaxes rule 32 only where the ASV writes a single relativizer — which 4:11, 4:16, 4:24, 4:25 and 4:36 all do correctly.

Candidates checked and rejected as source- or ASV-licensed rather than splits: ἐνώπιον → before (4:10) against → in the sight of (4:19), which rule 71 decides on the ASV's phrasing; the negation family, where 4:12 empties οὐκ before a negative indefinite (rule 41), 4:34 keeps neither on οὐδέ before a positively rendered τις (rule 69), and 4:32 splits οὐδὲ εἷς because two English words are written; the supplied complementizer, on the expanded non-finite complement at 4:5, 4:17, 4:30 and 4:32 without exception (rule 85); the supplied juncture and, on the finite verb it introduces at 4:18, 4:19, 4:34 and 4:37 (rule 88); πνεῦμα, where 4:8 and 4:25 give the supplied determiner to the anarthrous noun (rules 51, 58) and 4:31 gives it to the article that stands there (rule 21); and ὑπάρχω with a dative of possession, aligned at 4:32 where the ASV writes he and unrepresented at 4:37 where having writes nothing for it.

The preverb question is the chapter's recurring one and is settled consistently: together rides inside συνάγω's unit at 4:27 and 4:31, further realizes προσ- at 4:21, here realizes παρα- at 4:10, forth ἐκ- at 4:30, aside ἀπ- at 4:15, against ἀντι- at 4:14; and where the compound governs a bare dative (4:1, 4:3) the English upon or on realizes the case government and rides with the pronoun under rule 106's closing clause. ACT.4.26 is the one place a following ἐπὶ τὸ αὐτό competes for the single English together, and it takes it as a noncompositional pair with the article unrepresented, following MAT.22.34 and ACT.2.44. That collision is what the amendment below records.

BSB disagreements: none is a genuine error. Eleven are articles the ASV realizes nowhere — before a name (4:10, 4:19), displaced by a possessive (4:25, 4:35, 4:37), emptied by an attributive demonstrative (4:16, 4:27), determinerless (4:3, 4:36), nominalizing an articular infinitive (4:30), or inside a noncompositional unit (4:26, rule 93). The remaining four are ἐπί left unrepresented as pleonastic in ἐπὶ πλεῖον (4:17, rule 34), εἰς absorbed into was made the head (4:11, rule 36), οὐκ emptied by a following negative indefinite (4:12, rule 41, which says in terms that the report is not a correction), and αὐτῷ at 4:37, where the ASV's having a field writes no word for the dative possessor. No accepted edge was changed to improve the rate.

Two single-verse judgments were checked and left standing, both already carrying review notes: ACT.4.35's split of according / as between καθότι and ἄν, which rule 50 forces by naming an unrepresented ἄν the one particle whose disagreement report is itself a correction; and ACT.4.32's added of them, whose licensing token πλήθους is already spent on multitude (rule 103), the fold onto εἷς remaining defensible and named in the unit's note.
